page: Microsoft Azure D32ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. A key hardware inclusion is the 1890 GB of local NVMe storage, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU metrics and single-threaded gzip compression rates placing in the top 10% of tested instances. Multi-core performance, measured by stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores, ranks in the strong top 25% tier. Cryptographic and vector operations are accelerated by hardware support for AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, AES, and SHA_NI instruction sets. Memory bandwidth and database operations, such as Redis SET, perform within the average range.

Given the 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and substantial local storage, this instance provides a balanced resource profile suitable for relational databases, web serving, and moderate data processing pipelines. It also demonstrates strong performance in small-scale language model inference, particularly in text generation. The inclusion of a large local disk alongside dedicated CPU resources offers high resource density, making it a qualitatively cost-effective choice for workloads requiring fast local scratch space without the need for dedicated GPU hardware.
